_label: Evidence archive: the Flickr account's own creation date (4 March 2008)

identified_by.content: Evidence archive: the Flickr account's own creation date (4 March 2008)

content: Two fields in the studio's own Flickr data export, requested and downloaded in 2026, fix the creation of the account 24377024@N07 (username sundog358) to 2008-03-04 22:31:26: the account's own 'join_date' field, and the timestamp on an automated welcome message sent by the platform to that account at the same moment. Neither is the studio's own record of the date; both are generated by Flickr's own systems. This is the earliest account-creation date, fixed by any platform's own record, that this collection holds.

referred_to_by.content: The export and how it is held. The relevant files sit inside 'data/72157725696141408_a7a8f8ddb54c_part1.zip', one of the container zips of the studio's Flickr data export, SHA-256 e1e196323ce59019e731a610437c27239df57e8e929c54fd1abf54cf54142297. Within it, 'account_profile.json', 4,800 bytes, SHA-256 ec57c51e4a0da9faeb95925e109e63fad0f558a5ecc9338a353a686416899a47, carries the field 'join_date': '2008-03-04 22:31:26', alongside the account's real name and its Artist Bio, the same undated text already held on the studio's Tumblr and Twitter/X profiles. 'received_flickrmail_part001.json', 1,810 bytes, SHA-256 e09cbad07e3bec811980775edf6dff7323aae1640b436fb9b10fc9a88cea47ff, holds two messages in total ever received by this account; the first, id 72157604046527156, subject 'Welcome to Flickr!', addressed to 'sundog358', sent by Flickr's own system rather than by a user, gives 'date_sent': '2008-03-04 22:31:26', the same value to the second as the profile's join_date field. The two fields are generated by different parts of Flickr's own systems and agree exactly; this collection treats that agreement as evidence the value is Flickr's own record rather than an artefact of one field. Flickr's export does not state the timezone of these timestamps.

What this does and does not show. It fixes when the account was created; it says nothing about when the Artist Bio, or any other profile text, was first written into it, since Flickr's export carries no edit history for profile fields and the bio could have been added at any point after 2008-03-04. This is the same limit already stated for the account-creation dates of the studio's LinkedIn and X/Twitter accounts, both set out in their own records. Unlike those two, which sit three weeks apart in a cluster of autumn 2011, this account predates them by three and a half years and is, at present, the earliest account-creation date fixed by any platform's own record that this collection holds; the MySpace account is estimated to be older still, from late April to 8 May 2007, but that estimate rests on the position of a numeric identifier relative to other accounts' captured dates, not on a record the platform generated for this account itself.

Redaction. The second and only other message the account ever received, dated 2018-08-21, is spam advertising an unrelated third-party site; it is not from Flickr's own system, names no one connected to this collection, and its content is not reproduced here beyond noting that it exists and is irrelevant. The welcome message quoted above is boilerplate text sent identically to every new Flickr account at the time and names no third party.
